unreleased.text: The jogging pill is easy to read now (dark text on amber), and it grows open on a spring when you start jogging and shrinks away smoothly when you stop, instead of popping in and out.

Motion starts where you tap: switching tabs or opening a page from the island at the bottom spreads the new screen up from that button, a page opened from a pill at the top comes down from it, and Back gathers it back into the spot it came from. Everything moves slow-fast-slow with a little spring at the end. Chips and island buttons change shape when pressed, every tap gives a light buzz, and scrolling has a subtle cloth-like feel: the side away from your thumb trails a touch behind and settles when you stop.

Scrolling feels like weighted cloth: as you scroll, the side away from your thumb trails behind (up to 3°), and when you stop it swings back a little past flat and settles. Tuned on the Cloth Scroll Lab test page.

Settings: all reminders are now on one Reminders page, in sections: Logging, Coach, Movement and Water. “Theme & colour” is now “Look & feel”, with a new Motion section where you can turn cloth-like scrolling off or tune its strength, sensitivity, springiness and wobble (default: your tuning of 2.7°, 3.3, 0.25, no wobble).

Fixed: when GPS barely moved during a walk (indoors or a weak signal), the walk got a tiny distance, and the coach then said you were “shuffling or standing around”. Now, if the GPS distance would mean steps of just a few centimetres, the distance, pace and stride come from your steps × step length instead (marked ≈ with a note on the walk), and the coach is told the GPS failed, so it trusts your steps and cadence. This also fixes walks you’ve already recorded.

Steps by the hour now include the walks you record. Health Connect often gets a walk’s steps late (or not at all), so a recorded walk could show as 0 steps in its hour; now each hour shows whichever is higher, Health Connect’s count or the walk’s own steps in that hour, and recorded walks are highlighted in mint like the others.

While an update downloads, the progress bar now waves the whole time, like Android’s own Material 3 Expressive bars: the wave keeps rolling even when the download pauses, the bar glides to each new percentage, the wave flattens out near the start and the finish, and there’s a dot marking the end. If the size isn’t known yet, a wavy stretch keeps sweeping across the bar until it is.

items.text: Recording a walk or hike now starts with a race-style countdown: 3 · 2 · 1 · Go! with beeps (ting, tingg, tiiing, tuuut) and a buzz on each. Tapped Start by mistake? Press Cancel before Go and nothing is recorded.

While you jog, a big amber pill on the recording screen shows how long you’ve jogged and how far (“🏃 Jogged 1:15 · 210 m”). And any live number (pace, speed, cadence, stride) that stays clearly above your average for this walk for 3 seconds turns amber too, so you can see at a glance when you’re pushing.
Log food: the Log it button is now at the top, next to ✕, and the top of every sheet stays on screen as you scroll, so the button is never hidden behind the keyboard or the time picker.

Fixed: after the app updated overnight, an old reminder you’d tapped “Later” on (like Sunday’s breakfast) could pop up the next morning. Old snoozed reminders are now dropped, and a snoozed one is also dropped as soon as you log that thing.

One reminder per moment: when the coach has a tip for a meal (or a walk reminder) at the same time as a “Keep it going” habit, you now get just the tip instead of two notifications about the same meal.

When you’ve logged a cold, sore throat, cough or fever (today or yesterday), the coach now sticks to warm, soothing food: soups, dal, khichdi, hot sabji, warm eggs or paneer, haldi doodh, ginger tea, instead of dahi, chaas or anything cold, and still finds you warm protein. Tomorrow’s meal tips follow the same rule.

How long a walk took now reads in words, like “9 mins 15 secs” or “1 hr 4 mins 9 secs”, so it can’t be mistaken for a clock time like 9:15. This covers the walk page (moving and total time, with big numbers and small units), the recording pill and finish screen, jogs, and what the coach is told. Pace stays as min/km.

Every length of time is now in words: the live recording clock (“25 mins 03.45 secs”), the jogging pill (“Jogged 1 min 15 secs · 210 m”) and sleep (“7 hrs 30 mins”, “30 mins short of 7 hrs”), as well as walks.

Recording no longer waits on GPS: until it finds you (indoors it may not at all), distance, speed, pace and stride are worked out from your steps and step length, marked ≈ and “from steps”. When GPS finds you it takes over, and the distance you walked before that still counts, in the saved walk too. While it’s looking, you see how many satellites it has, e.g. “Finding GPS… 3/11 satellites”.

Walks find your location much faster: recording now uses Google’s location service, the same one Google Maps uses, which combines GPS with Wi-Fi, mobile towers and the phone’s motion sensors instead of waiting on the GPS chip alone. Rough Wi-Fi positions indoors aren’t drawn on the route, so indoor walking is counted from your steps.

Walk maps: drag to move, pinch (or double-tap) to zoom; 2 seconds after you let go the map glides back to the whole route. Points that GPS throws across the road near tall buildings (a sudden spike out and back) are now dropped from the route and from the distance, on your past walks too.

Logging food no longer waits for the AI: tap Log it and the meal is in straight away, marked “Working out macros…”, and its calories, protein, carbs and fat fill in a few seconds later while you carry on. If the AI can’t answer, the meal stays logged and shows “Macros failed · tap to retry”; if the app closes first, it finishes the next time you open it. Same for adding food to a past day.

The island at the bottom now changes with the screen. On a tab, the + does that page's main thing: Log food on Food, Start a walk on Fitness (or Back to the recording while one is running), Log weight on Progress; Home still opens the Log menu, and holding the + anywhere opens it too. Settings has no +. On a full-screen page the tabs make way for that page's own buttons, within thumb reach: In & out and Steps get Back, Earlier, Now and Later; a walk gets the previous and next walk (and Edit); the coach gets the day before and after, and the + becomes Get a fresh review, showing the loading shape while the coach thinks. The island morphs between the two on a spring.

Fixed: tapping a tab while In & out (or Steps, a walk or the coach) was open switched the tab hidden behind it. A tab tap now always takes you to that tab, and tapping the tab you're on takes you to its top.

Home-screen widgets: Steps, Calories burned, Calories eaten and In & out. Long-press your home screen → Widgets → Fitness Tracker. Each one changes what it shows as you resize it: Steps grows from a count in a scalloped shape to a wavy progress ring, your day hour by hour, today's walks and the week; Calories burned adds resting and moving, burn through the day and where it came from; Calories eaten goes from the Fuel ring to protein, carbs and fat and today's meals; In & out shows this week's eaten-versus-burned bars, the daily averages and the verdict, like the In & out page (from 2×2 up, so nothing gets left out). Small sizes shorten numbers to thousands, like 6.2k. Tapping a widget opens its page.

So the steps and calories burned widgets stay current while the app is closed, the app explains and then asks Health Connect for one more permission: reading your steps in the background (every 15 minutes, steps only, nothing leaves your phone). You can allow it later from Settings → Health Connect → Widgets.
Fixed: opening or closing a pill's card (like the coach's tips) flashed a big square for a moment. The card now unfolds down from the pills and folds back up into them.
Fixed: the “Get tomorrow’s plan” pill stayed up after you tapped it. It now goes away as soon as the coach starts reviewing your day, and doesn’t come back once the review is in.

When Google’s free AI is overloaded (“high demand”), the app now waits a moment and tries again, then uses the lighter free model, before giving up, so the coach’s review usually comes through anyway. If it still can’t, it says so in plain words. The same wait-and-retry applies to Claude when it’s busy.

In & out → Day now shows exactly how resting calories were worked out: your daily resting burn, and the weight (and which weigh-in it came from), height, age and sex it used. If any of these are guesses because they aren't set, it says so with a button to add them. Resting now uses the age from your profile.

The coach's meal tips, walk nudges and habit cheers now come 1 hour before your usual time (instead of 15 minutes), so there's time to plan lunch or get ready to walk. Never before you usually wake up. Choose 30 min, 1 h, 1 h 30 or 2 h in Settings → Logging reminders.

The second brisk walk is now “Walk after lunch”: the app learns how long after lunch you usually set off and times the nudge from lunch (from today's lunch if it's logged, so a late lunch moves it too). If you usually walk later in the day instead, it follows that. The coach also knows your usual walk times when it plans.

Settings → Logging reminders: every reminder now has its own timing under its switch. Sleep check-in 15 min–1 h 30 after you wake; each meal 30 min–1 h 30 after its usual time; bedtime 15–60 min before lights-out; the coach's meal tips 30 min–2 h before; brisk walks 15 min–1 h 30 before. The page is split into “Logging reminders” (after the usual time) and “Coach's reminders” (before it).

In & out → Day now has an Eaten card next to Burned, showing the day's food as calories: how much came at each meal, how much came from protein, carbs and fat, and the foods that brought the most calories.

In & out now shows whether the gap is healthy, not just which side is bigger. Each burned bar is split into what you burn at rest (faded) and by moving. A dashed line marks your resting burn, and an eaten bar turns red when you ate less than it. A dot under each day shows green for a healthy deficit (about 250–750 kcal), amber for a big one, red for over 1,000, blue for about even and pink for a surplus (judged against your goal of losing, keeping or gaining). The summary says your pace in kg a week and what it means.

The coach now opens full screen from anywhere: the Ask the coach cards on Home, Food, Food history and Fitness, the “Get tomorrow's plan” pill and its notification. The page grows out of what you tapped and shrinks back into it when you go back. While the coach thinks you see a morphing Material 3 Expressive loading shape and what it's working on, and the review's sections rise in one after another. The cards on each page now show a peek of the last review.

Motion across the app, Material 3 Expressive style: pages like Steps, a walk, In & out and the recording screen grow out of what you tapped and shrink back into it on Back (keeping your scroll position); switching tabs or Today/History fades through; sheets rise from the bottom and sink away; a pill grows into its card. Cards, rows and pills change shape when pressed, and the “working…” spinners are now the same morphing shape. Turn on Android's “Remove animations” to switch it all off.
About & updates: when the app was updated through Android's shell, it now says what that means (an app using Shizuku, or a computer over ADB) instead of just “Shell”.

A walk or hike being recorded now shows as a bright red pill pinned at the top of every page (with a blinking dot, distance and time), so it never scrolls away. Tap it to go back to the recording. “Version x is out” is a pinned pill on Home too, with ✕ to hide it.

Pills at the top for everything that needs you, each in its own colour and icon: 🍽️ log a meal (amber), 😴 log your sleep (violet), 🌙 bedtime (indigo), 🧠 the coach's tips and “get tomorrow's plan” (blue), 🚶 walk time (green), ⭐ keep a good habit going (pink). They appear once a reminder is due, even if you opened the app without tapping the notification or it was dismissed, and go away once it's done. Tap to act or open the full message; ✕ or Later hides one for 30 minutes.
Setup prompts are pills too (set your goals, add measurements, a goal weight, steps by the hour, show a route in Google Health): grey, on the page they belong to. ✕ hides one for a week.

New Burned card on Home, under Fuel: how many calories you've burned so far and where they came from (resting, walks, everyday steps, workout, and digesting food), with a coloured bar like Fuel's macros. Its tag shows how far you are into a deficit or surplus.

Tap Burned for the new In & out page: what you ate and what you burned, side by side for every day of a week or month, and for the average day of each week of a quarter or each month of a year, against your eating target. It adds up the deficit or surplus and roughly what that means in kg.
Food → History: each day's food is now split into Breakfast, Lunch, Snack and Dinner like Today, with each meal's calories and protein and a + to add to that meal on that day.
Settings → About & updates now shows when the app was last updated and which app on your phone did it (for example an app store, or Android's installer if you opened an APK).

Recording a walk or hike: every number has an icon next to its name (⏱️ Time, 👟 Steps, ⚡ Pace, 🎵 Cadence, 📏 Stride…), the same icons as the after-walk page. The name above and the line below each number now use the same text style, and every row is evenly spaced.

The coach now plans tomorrow. When you ask for the day's review, it also sets reminders for the next day, each 15 minutes before your usual time: what to eat before breakfast, lunch, snack and dinner, your morning brisk walk (and a second walk when it asks for one), and a cheer to repeat something you did well. Its tips also show up in the water and move reminders. The review card lists what it set.
Morning walk reminder: if you usually walk in the morning, a nudge comes 15 minutes before your usual time (skipped once you've walked). Tapping 🚶 Start walk begins recording.

After dinner is logged and the day hasn't been reviewed yet, a reminder asks you to get the coach's review, so tomorrow's reminders can be set from it. Coach reviews are now also kept when the app is closed. Both switches are in Settings → Logging reminders, under “From the coach”.

Recording a walk or hike: “🏃 Jogging” now shows about 3 seconds after you start jogging (it used to take 15-20 seconds) and goes off about 3 seconds after you slow back to walking. The live steps-a-minute and “now” pace also react much faster, and Jogging no longer flickers on and off.

Recording a walk or hike: Pace, Speed and Cadence now show what you're doing right now in big, with your average for the walk underneath. When you're paused or standing still, the big number is your average and says so.

Recording a walk or hike: show as many big numbers as you like, not just 2. Big ones sit two to a row (an odd one out gets a whole row), and any number of small ones go below the map. Choose them under ⚙️ Layout.

After a walk or hike: new “How it went over time” charts for pace, speed, cadence and stride, minute by minute, each with its average. Tap a point for its value. This works for walks you've already recorded too.
Recording a walk or hike: Stride now also shows your current stride in big, with the walk's average underneath, like Pace, Speed and Cadence.
Water: each drink in the list now has an ✎ edit button. Change how much you drank and what time, then Save. Health Connect gets the corrected entry too.

New date picker in the app's own style, instead of Android's old grey calendar: the day in big type, quick picks like Yesterday and 2 days ago, and a month grid where days ahead are greyed out. Used for logging food on a past day and for the exact start of a symptom (with the clock-style time picker).

Opening the app: the logo on the loading screen now has the same size and spot as Android's opening logo, so it no longer jumps up and shrinks as the app loads. This takes effect from the second time you open the app after updating, once the app has measured where it sits on your screen.

Walk and hike charts: the height line no longer starts with a big jump. GPS height is often far off for the first few seconds, so those heights are now left out, and single wrong readings are smoothed away, so climb and descent come out closer to the real thing. This fixes walks you've already recorded too.
Top speed on walks and hikes now counts only a speed you kept up for at least 10 seconds, so a GPS jump no longer shows a 22 km/h top speed on a walk.

One coach everywhere: Ask the coach on Home, Food, Food history and Fitness now gives the same full review of the day, with sections for food, walks, workout, and sleep, water & feeling, plus a top win, what to do next and recovery. It keeps the gut and illness checks, and a review you already asked for opens straight away (↻ gets a fresh one).

The walk and hike recording screen is yours to arrange: tap ⚙️ Layout and pick up to 2 big numbers and 6 small ones (time, steps, distance, pace, speed, cadence, stride, calories, and climb and height on hikes). Walks and hikes keep their own layout.

While recording: the time runs like a stopwatch with hundredths and shows when you started; a pill shows the time now; cadence, speed and pace show what you're doing right now as well as the average; Pause and Finish float where the menu island usually is.
Pace now reads like 13:36 min/km everywhere.

Short jogs inside a walk are spotted from your speed and steps (140+ steps a minute, or 7.5+ km/h). A 🏃 Jogging pill shows while you jog, and the walk's page lists each jog, shows it in amber on the map and counts it in calories.

The coach's walk analysis goes deeper: pace (min/km and km/h), cadence and stride against your last 7 days, what they say about your steps, any short jogs, and concrete targets for pace, cadence and stride.

With sips, gulps & glasses on, the quick water buttons are always +1 gulp and +1 glass (on Home, in the amount picker and on the reminder), since hardly anyone drinks a whole bottle in one go. Bottles are still in Add water.

Smarter move reminders: they now come when you've most likely been sitting with your phone (using it, or with it in your pocket), not when it was just lying on a table while you were up and about. Walking a few steps, even carrying the phone to another room, starts the sitting time again. If you were on your phone the whole time, the reminder says so.

Water and move reminders got a sense of humour: each one picks a fact from today or yesterday and has fun with it, like “Chicken biryani brought the salt 🧂 Water is the cleanup crew”, “That 980-kcal lunch wants a walk 🍛→🚶” or “Doomscroll detected 📱 Swap 5 minutes of scrolling for 5 minutes of strolling.”

Log water the way you drink it: in Settings → Water reminders, choose Sips, gulps & glasses. The buttons then say +1 gulp, +1 glass, 1 bottle, and the reminder's buttons say 1 glass and 1 bottle. Your gulp size comes from your weight (and gender if set). Everything is still saved in ml.

Water buttons learn your habits: the amounts you log most (recent days count more) come first on the Home water card, in the amount picker, at the top of Add water, and on the reminder's buttons. Start logging gulps and +1 gulp moves to the front within a few days.

Bedtime reminders: 30 minutes before lights-out, with the reason and a bit of fun, like “Sleep debt collector calling 💸 Last night was only 5 h 10 min. To be up at 6:10 AM like last Monday with 8 h 15 min of sleep, lights out by 9:55 PM.” Tomorrow's wake-up time comes from the same weekday last week, else this morning, else your usual time. The sleep you need comes from your age (8 h up to 25, 7 h 30 after), plus 30 min after a short night and 15 min after a hike or a hard day. Turn it on or off in Settings → Logging reminders.
Food → History is back to food only: each day's meals and how you felt. Walks, hikes, water, sleep, workouts and weight stay on the Home timeline.

Fixed the weekly review failing with “reply was cut off”, with Claude and with the free AI: when an answer runs out of room, the app now asks again straight away with twice the room, and the review starts with more space.

When an update is ready, the Download & install button is now at the top, above the list of what's new. The newest version's pictures stay in What's new (Settings → About & updates) after you install it.

Food → History now shows each day's full timeline in time order: meals together with walks and hikes, workouts, water, sleep, weight and how you felt, plus that day's steps and calories burned. Days with activity but no food show up too.
A walk or hike you're recording shows on today's timeline as it happens. Tap it to go back to the live screen. Hikes have a 🥾 boot on the timeline.
Timelines on Home and in Food → History show the newest entry at the top.
The app icon follows your phone's light or dark mode: a white background with a deeper colour in light mode, black with the bright colour in dark mode.
The Steps page buttons now read Start a walk and Start a hike, and the Fitness page has ▶ Walk and ▶ Hike instead of a plain Start.

One opening screen instead of two: the app's loading screen now continues Android's own splash with the same apple in the same place and colour (your accent colour if App icon in accent colour is on), white in light mode and black in dark mode. A wavy progress line shows if loading takes a moment.

Settings → Goals shows your goals as plain numbers. Tap Edit goals to change them, then Save (or Cancel). Nothing changes until you save, and the suggested goals fill in the fields for you to check first.

When the weekly review or the coach can't answer, it now says why (for example, the free AI has used up its allowance for now, or there's no internet) instead of always blaming the connection. The weekly review also retries once by itself if the AI sends back a blank or broken reply.

Record a walk: tap Start a walk (Steps page, Fitness or +). The app records your route with GPS, plus distance, time, pace and steps, even with the screen off. A notification shows the progress. Pause, resume, then Finish to save or discard.
Each recorded walk has its own page: the route on a map, moving and total time, average pace and speed, steps, cadence, stride, calories, climb, top speed, pace for each km and an elevation chart.
Walks found from your phone's steps open their own page too, with time, steps, cadence and calories. Distance, pace and stride are estimated, and there's no map.
Recorded walks go to Health Connect with their route, steps and distance, so they show in Google Health. Tap Allow once on a walk's page to share routes.

Google Drive backup, like WhatsApp: in Settings → Data & backup, sign in with Google once. The app then backs up by itself (daily, weekly or monthly, on Wi-Fi or also mobile data) to a hidden folder in your own Drive, keeping the last 30. Back up now any time, or restore any backup on a new phone.

The coach now looks at everything you log, everywhere it appears (Home, food history, workout review and weekly analysis): every meal with its macros, water, sleep, weight, how you felt, walks (recorded, found from your steps or added by hand), all your steps and workouts. It weighs what you ate against what you burned. The coach card also shows on days with no meals logged.

Logging reminders: a friendly good-morning check-in asks how you slept ("Lazy Sunday morning, Yash?", "New week!", or about yesterday: a late dinner, a long walk, a workout). A little after your usual breakfast, lunch, snack and dinner times you get a nudge if you haven't logged yet, with protein and calories left for today. Tap to log straight away, or Later to be asked again in 30 minutes. Your usual times are learned from when you log. Turn each one on or off in Settings → Logging reminders.
Fixed the water glass: when it was more than about 60% full, the water floated with a gap at the bottom. It now fills right down to the bottom, in the small glass and the big one.

Record a hike: tap 🥾 Hike on the Steps page (or Start a hike in +). While you hike you see distance, time, pace, steps, climb so far, your height above sea level, speed and a live height chart. It works with no mobile signal; only the map background needs internet.

Each hike has its own page: the route, an elevation profile, a speed chart, elevation gain and loss, highest and lowest point, climbing speed (metres up an hour), the steepest slope, moving time and rest time, pace and climb for each km, steps, stride and calories that count the climb. Hikes go to Health Connect as hiking.
Climb is measured with your phone's air-pressure sensor when it has one, which is much steadier than GPS height. On Android 14 and newer, heights are above sea level.

A new logo: an apple with a lightning bolt, for food as energy. It's one simple shape, so it's easy to spot in the notification bar. The home-screen icon is cyan; to make it match your accent colour, turn on App icon in accent colour in Settings → Theme & colour.
While the big glass fills after logging from a reminder, the small glass on the Water card stays hidden until the big one lands in its place.
Water reminder buttons (250 ml / 500 ml) now log the drink without opening the app, and the notification changes to show it was logged and your total for today.
Tapping the water reminder itself opens the app and asks how much you drank: a glass, a bottle or another amount. Then the big glass fills with that amount.
Water and move reminders show the app's icon, with a water or walking picture inside the notification, so they're easy to spot.
The app icon now matches your own custom accent colour too. There are 36 icon colours (your 12 presets plus a full colour wheel), and the app picks the closest the way your eye sees colour.

Food history: the coloured bar under each day now has a title (Where the calories came from) and labels: protein, carbs and fat with their share and grams. Meal tags spell out protein, carbs and fat instead of P, C and F.

Step charts show the count on every bar. Tap a month in Year to open that month, and a day in Week or Month to see it hour by hour. Progress trend charts write the values on short ranges, and you can tap any point to see its value and date.
Updates download and install inside the app, with a progress bar. No browser tab needed.
See what's new in each version, with pictures, in Settings → About & updates.
After an update, the app shows what changed the first time you open it.
Previous versions are listed one below another with their changes.
Move reminders: if you've barely moved for a while (you choose 30 min to 2 h, and the hours), you get a nudge to take a short walk. Turn it on in Settings → Move reminders.
Water: a drop falls into the glass when you tap +250 or +500. When you log from a reminder notification, a big glass fills in the middle of the screen and then shrinks into the small one.

Steps by the hour: tap the Move card on Home to see today's steps as a chart, with your walks found and named for you (for example Morning walk, Brisk evening walk, Night stroll). No need to log walks yourself.
The Steps page has Day, Week, Month and Year views, with a goal line, your best day and totals.
Calories burned now count all your steps, not just logged walks and workouts. Each walk shows its own calories.
Update downloads use Android's downloader, so they no longer get stuck at 100%.
Fixed meal macros failing when the AI replied in words instead of numbers (for example, meals with cabbage).
Works with both the free Gemini AI and Claude.
The project is now public. Anyone can download the app from GitHub Releases.
The app checks for updates when you open it, and Home shows a banner when a new version is out.
Settings → About & updates has a Check for updates button.
The coach's bullet-point tips show as a proper list.
A first-time setup that collects your name, body, goal, daily targets, AI choice and phone connections. Every page can be skipped.
Settings grouped by category: Profile, Body, Goals, AI, Water reminders, Health Connect, Theme & colour, Data & backup.
A free AI (Gemini) works out of the box. Claude with your own key is still an option.
Health Connect reads your phone's steps, and shares meals, water, walks, workouts, weight and sleep with Google Health.
The app icon follows your accent colour.
Press back again to exit.
Prompts appear when a feature needs details you haven't given yet.
Fixed the body-fat formula, which read about 6 points too high.
The first Android app: the floating island stays put, the back button works, and water reminders arrive with the app closed.
Your data is stored on the phone and kept by Android's own backup.
